content.text: A PR is here:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo-module-auth-webac/pull/39
We should discuss the contents of
./src/main/resources/root-acl.rdf
In order to be correct, the associated PR should include an implementation of the acl:Control mode
, based on yesterday's Sprint conversation, is your above comment still true?
you are correct, an implementation of acl:Control is not necessary at this point.
Please either create some documentation for Fedora administrators on how to use this feature, or create a new ticket for said documentation.
Pending response to code review comments.
PR has been updated to address code review comments. The default authorization also now denies access to resources (rather than granting them to the foaf:Agent agent).
A related issue has been created to address documenting this feature:
https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-1806
More code review comments
The open question now is whether the system ACL file should use internal or external identifiers for acl:accessTo triples.
It currently expects this:
<> acl:accessTo <info:fedora/>
But it could be changed to this:
<> acl:accessTo <
http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/
There are pros and cons either way, and I don't have a strong opinion one way or the other.
Looks good, pending code comment update.
I have attempted to clarify the code a bit – the confusing bit was pulled out into its own function (with its own comment), and the relevant inline comment was clarified.
Resolved with:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo-module-auth-webac/commit/7d9cf0d466bf7be2ddea7415a308bacdc0932d8a

This is a ticket to enforce ACL controls on ACL resources for non-admin agents. This has two parts: the first is to implement the acl:Control mode, which controls read/write access to ACLs. The second part is to have a file-based backstop (expressed in ACL rdf) for ACLs that don't contain (and whose parents don't contain) the acl:accessControl property.

comments.body:
A PR is here: https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo-module-auth-webac/pull/39

We should discuss the contents of ./src/main/resources/root-acl.rdf
In order to be correct, the associated PR should include an implementation of the acl:Control mode
Unknown, based on yesterday's Sprint conversation, is your above comment still true?
Andrew Woods you are correct, an implementation of acl:Control is not necessary at this point.
Please either create some documentation for Fedora administrators on how to use this feature, or create a new ticket for said documentation.

PR has been updated to address code review comments. The default authorization also now denies access to resources (rather than granting them to the foaf:Agent agent).

A related issue has been created to address documenting this feature: https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-1806

The open question now is whether the system ACL file should use internal or external identifiers for acl:accessTo triples.

It currently expects this:

<> acl:accessTo <info:fedora/>

But it could be changed to this:

<> acl:accessTo <http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/>

There are pros and cons either way, and I don't have a strong opinion one way or the other.
I have attempted to clarify the code a bit – the confusing bit was pulled out into its own function (with its own comment), and the relevant inline comment was clarified.
